rationale: Acceptance did not run (no spec/story available) so confidence is low; edge-case lens was the only applicable lens under the compact profile and ran clean. 2.3 verification confirmed three genuine defects in the newly-added project-default-fetch effect in ChatPromptLlmSelector.tsx (stale state on leaving a project chat, a race on rapid project switches, and an uncleared default on fetch failure) — all in-scope for this change per git history. One edge-case candidate (resolveInitialLlmModelType.ts future-enum fallthrough) was dismissed: the typed effective_llm_model_source union only allows 'assistant' | 'project_default' | null, so the flagged branch is unreachable under the current type contract. No defer findings; standards review was not expected for this profile.

findings.title: Stale project default survives leaving a project chat
findings.problem: The project-default fetch effect only guards `if (!currentChat?.projectId) return` — when currentChat.projectId transitions to undefined (switching to a non-project chat), the effect exits without resetting projectDefaultModelId, so the previous project's default id remains in state.
findings.impact: defaultModel later checks `if (projectDefaultModelId)` against the now-global modelsToDisplay list; if a global model shares the same id as the stale project default, it gets wrongly marked as the live default/recommended model.
findings.recommendation: Clear projectDefaultModelId (set to null) in the early-return branch when currentChat?.projectId is falsy, not just skip the fetch.

findings.title: No guard against a stale project-default fetch response
findings.problem: The effect that calls projectsStore.getProject(currentChat.projectId) has no guard against the user switching currentChat.projectId again before the in-flight request resolves — there is no AbortController, cancellation flag, or project-id comparison on resolution.
findings.impact: A stale response for a previously-selected project can overwrite projectDefaultModelId after the user has already switched to a different project, temporarily flagging the wrong model as the live default for the new project.
findings.recommendation: Capture the projectId at fetch start (or use a ref/cleanup flag) and ignore the response if currentChat.projectId no longer matches when the promise resolves.

findings.title: Fetch failure leaves stale default uncleared
findings.problem: The catch block in the project-default fetch effect only logs the error (console.error) and never resets projectDefaultModelId.
findings.impact: If a fetch for project B fails after a prior successful fetch for project A set a default, the UI keeps showing project A's stale default model id for project B instead of falling back to no default.
findings.recommendation: Call setProjectDefaultModelId(null) in the catch block alongside the existing console.error.
